attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack retrospective, written in the first person.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the hedge 'appear to have been confirmed' and the insider-comments basis. Reading the months as Nov–Dec 2024 is reasonable for a post dated Jan 1, 2025.

contract.note: The contract correctly declines to strip the hedge. The claim is a tentative self-assessment with no confirmation standard, so no binary test is fair.

reviews.rationale: The statement is hedged ('appear to have been confirmed') and amounts to a tentative judgment that his past predictions were vindicated. Under policy, graded or hedged language is not scored. The packet rightly offers no outcome evidence. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person statement on his Substack.

semantics.note: Faithful firm observation that the named weaknesses persist. 'Etc' and the priority references are rightly not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading (significant remaining weaknesses, not total absence) is ordinary and fair. Using Q4 2024 as the window fits a Jan 1, 2025 post. Requiring evidence in all three domains is reasonable.

evidence.note: Oct 2024 peer-reviewed evaluation finds consistent familiar vs unseen composition gaps, GPT-4 included. Supports the compositionality weakness, though only for one task family.

Oct 2024 SimpleQA release: frontier models including GPT-4o score under 40% and hallucinations remain an open problem. This is a company disclosure, but it describes a multi-model benchmark and cuts against the company's own interest.
Oct 2024 GSM-Symbolic v1 shows performance drops from value changes and irrelevant clauses across SOTA models. Supports the reasoning-fragility weakness.
Dec 2024 ARC result for o3 preview shows major progress on novel tasks, but it does not show any named domain was reliably solved. Qualifies the claim without contradicting it.

reviews.rationale: Contemporary Q4 2024 evaluations document recurring weaknesses in all three domains: compositionality (e1), factuality (e2) and reasoning (e3). The o3 ARC result (e4) shows real progress but not reliable solutions, so the contradiction condition is not met. Supported on the plain reading, with limited coverage of models and tasks.
